designs.title: The Goat Prelate
designs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: isolated original Gothic cathedral stone statue design, image reference for later CL3D reconstruction in SECHA / Red Descent.
Primary request: a magnificent, sinister medieval cathedral sculpture with the oppressive occult atmosphere of the first Diablo, rendered as believable carved sculpture rather than a living fantasy character. Original design.
Style/materials: masterfully sculpted, centuries-old grey limestone, restrained warm grey variation, chisel facets, deeply worked drapery and undercuts, chipped arrises, worn fingers and muzzle details, sparse grime in recesses. Intricate Gothic craftsmanship at large and medium scales, strong architectural mass, no uniformly noisy surface. All robes, horns, wings and accessories are CARVED STONE.
Composition: ONE complete isolated sculpture and its attached modest integral base, all edges and base visible with 10 percent margin. Gentle three-quarter view only 10-15 degrees off front, human-eye camera, mild perspective, tall portrait framing unless the subject is naturally squat. Readable front and side thickness. One view of one object.
Lighting: neutral diffuse studio lighting with a soft raking side light to reveal carving, clear midtones and readable cavities, no blown highlights, no dramatic colored light, no cast ground-shadow plane.
Background: genuinely transparent alpha, including visible openings.
Construction: substantial joined forms that could be carved and reconstructed as one robust 3D object; accessories visibly connected to hands and torso; thick, plausible stone horns and wings. Distinct silhouette, meaningful asymmetry and localized wear.
Avoid: a cathedral scene or architectural backdrop, floor plane, extra disconnected props, repeated figures, contact sheets, multiple angles, labels, text, watermarks, living flesh, fabric garments, metal armor, glossy resin, toy/cartoon proportions, modern fantasy game armor, gore, magical glowing effects, excessive hair-fine ornament.
Subject: A towering 2.7 m enthroned goat-headed prelate. Immense thick curling ram horns encircle a stern long caprine face; a narrow Gothic mitre rises between them. Upright on a squat high-backed throne with a pointed tracery silhouette and one broken finial. Heavy ceremonial stone robes fall into deep angular folds. Both claw-like hands rest on closed arms of the throne; a small sealed book is carved into the lap. Imposing frontal pyramidal mass, approximately 1.0 m wide and 0.85 m deep, one chipped horn tip, the empty eyes are sculpted dark hollows. The throne is integral to the statue, no separate scene.

Intricate Gothic craftsmanship at large and medium scales, strong architectural mass, no uniformly noisy surface. All robes, horns, wings and accessories are CARVED STONE.
Composition: ONE complete isolated sculpture and its attached modest integral base, all edges and base visible with 10 percent margin. Gentle three-quarter view only 10-15 degrees off front, human-eye camera, mild perspective, tall portrait framing unless the subject is naturally squat. Readable front and side thickness. One view of one object.
Lighting: neutral diffuse studio lighting with a soft raking side light to reveal carving, clear midtones and readable cavities, no blown highlights, no dramatic colored light, no cast ground-shadow plane.
Background: genuinely transparent alpha, including visible openings.
Construction: substantial joined forms that could be carved and reconstructed as one robust 3D object; accessories visibly connected to hands and torso; thick, plausible stone horns and wings. Distinct silhouette, meaningful asymmetry and localized wear.
Avoid: a cathedral scene or architectural backdrop, floor plane, extra disconnected props, repeated figures, contact sheets, multiple angles, labels, text, watermarks, living flesh, fabric garments, metal armor, glossy resin, toy/cartoon proportions, modern fantasy game armor, gore, magical glowing effects, excessive hair-fine ornament.
Subject: A 2.4 m tall limestone funerary bishop with a clearly sculpted skull face under a tall chipped Gothic mitre. Broad ceremonial cope drapes from the shoulders and joins the feet in a solid pillar. The arms hold a large oval ossuary shield against the chest, carved with three shallow skull reliefs, no separate bones. Thick gloved stone hands and massive layered hems. Anatomical skull is a dry stone carving, no flesh or gore. Solemn and menacing medieval cathedral memorial, no horns, no wings, no weapon.
